title: Jerome on Micah 1:1
body: “Micah the Morasthite a joint heir with Christ announces the spoiling of the daughter of the robber and lays siege against her, because she has smitten the jawbone of the judge of Israel.”
author: Jerome, Letter 53, to Paulinus
bodyEs: “Miqueas de Morasti, coheredero con Cristo, anuncia el despojo de la hija del ladrón y pone sitio contra ella, porque ha herido la quijada del juez de Israel.”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 3:1
body: “Then is the charge against you the heavier, because the people believed, and ye believed not. They acted like men that knew the Law; how then are they accursed?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Entonces la acusación contra ustedes es más grave, porque el pueblo creyó, y ustedes no creyeron. Obraron como hombres que conocían la Ley; ¿cómo, pues, son malditos?”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 5:2
body: “He praises and approves the man, because he had said, "Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?" and yet he ought to have been blamed.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Alaba y aprueba al hombre, porque había dicho: "¿De Nazaret puede haber algo de bueno?", y sin embargo debía haber sido reprendido.”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 5:2
body: “And observe, I pray you, his manner of declining, how gentle he has made it, and in the form of a question. For he said not, "Galilee produces no good"; but how said he?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Y observa, te ruego, su manera de rehusar, cuán suave la ha hecho, y en forma de pregunta. Porque no dijo: "Galilea no produce nada bueno"; sino ¿cómo dijo?”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 6:2
body: “Having spoken of Bishops and Deacons, of men, and women, of widows and elders, and of all others, and having shown how great was the authority of a Bishop, now he was speaking of judgment, he has added, "I charge thee before God and the Lord Jesus Christ and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality." Thus fearfully he charges him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Habiendo hablado de obispos y diáconos, de hombres y mujeres, de viudas y ancianos, y de todos los demás, y habiendo mostrado cuán grande era la autoridad de un obispo, ahora que hablaba del juicio, ha añadido: "Te encargo delante de Dios y del Señor Jesucristo y de los ángeles escogidos, que guardes estas cosas sin preferir a uno antes que a otro, no haciendo nada por parcialidad." Así de temible lo encarga.”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 6:3
body: “Having made this defence of himself, (for he frequently defends himself, without being ashamed; for if God doth so, saying, "O My people, what have I done unto thee?" (Micah vi.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Habiendo hecho esta defensa de sí mismo (porque con frecuencia se defiende, sin avergonzarse; porque si Dios lo hace, diciendo: "Pueblo mío, ¿qué te he hecho?" (Mi. 6.”

title: John Chrysostom on Micah 6:3
body: “Then because the term "philosophy" has an appearance of dignity, he added, "and vain deceit." For there is also a good deceit; such as many have been deceived by, which one ought not even to call a deceit at all.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Luego, porque el término "filosofía" tiene apariencia de dignidad, añadió: "y vano engaño". Porque también hay un engaño bueno; tal como muchos han sido engañados por él, al cual ni siquiera se debería llamar engaño.”
